To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the human brain is capable of regulating its energy metabolism to support the higher energy requirement during brain activation, and the regulation is achieved through the highly correlated neuroenergetics changes in the ATP production pathways.
the human brain at resting-state can regulate ATP energy production in response to visual stimulation, and that the neuroenergetic regulation is associated with large interindividual variability.

(1) ATP energy metabolism is highly correlated with the evoked neural activity, (2) the ATP production rate is tightly coupled with ATP hydrolysis, (3) there is large individual variance in the neuroenergetics responses to a stimulus, (4) the neuroenergetic response is associated with the changes of intracellular [H+], [Mg2+], and Ca2+.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the human brain regulates its energy metabolism and what the consequences of this are in terms of neuronal activity.
the development of novel quantitative imaging techniques for the assessment of the energy metabolism in the human brain.
the development of new methods for the non-invasive assessment of the energy metabolism in the living human brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study provides a new tool to quantitatively assess brain ATP energy metabolism in vivo.
the human brain is a highly dynamic system, and that its energy regulation is tightly coupled to its function.
the human brain has a highly efficient mechanism for regulating ATP production rates to meet higher energy demand at the evoked state, and this mechanism is highly individualized.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed an imaging tool to quantify ATP production rates and intracellular pH and Mg2+ concentrations in the human brain, and used this tool to investigate how the brain energy metabolism is regulated in response to neuronal activity and how the brain energy state is associated with individual differences in brain functions.
we have developed an in vivo neuroimaging technique that allows quantitative measurement of ATP production rates in the human brain, which is essential for brain functions.

the human brain can effectively regulate ATP energy metabolism at working-state through highly coordinated neuroenergetic responses, with large individual variations in the responses and significant reductions of intracellular H+ and Mg2+ during the stimulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain can dynamically regulate its ATP production to meet the energy demands of the neurons.

we have developed a quantitative imaging tool for measuring ATP production rates in human brain, which has the potential to be applied to study neuroenergetic state changes in various physiological and pathophysiological conditions.

the brain can effectively regulate its ATP production rate in response to the increased energy demand during visual stimulation, and that this regulation is highly correlated with the neurophysiological changes, indicating the importance of the ATP synthesis reaction in supporting the evoked neuronal activity.
